pharm: Reversible inhibitor of gastric and pancreatic lipases acting locally in the GI lumen to block dietary fat absorption; minimal systemic absorption.
quick: 120 mg PO TID with each fat-containing meal (OTC 60 mg TID)
Take with or up to 1 h after each main meal containing fat
Caution; rare severe liver injury reported
Weight, BMI; LFTs if symptomatic; INR if on warfarin
summary: Orlistat is a GI lipase inhibitor used for weight loss and weight maintenance in overweight/obese adults alongside a reduced-calorie, low-fat diet. It blocks absorption of about 25-30% of dietary fat, which is then passed in the stool. Effect is local with negligible systemic absorption. GI effects (oily stool, flatus, fecal urgency) are common and worse with high-fat meals. Reduces absorption of fat-soluble vitamins, so a bedtime multivitamin is advised. Available OTC as 60 mg (alli) and by prescription as 120 mg (Xenical).
indications: Obesity management - weight loss and weight maintenance with a reduced-calorie diet (BMI >=30, or >=27 with risk factors such as hypertension, diabetes, dyslipidemia)
Reduction of the risk for weight regain after prior weight loss
OTC use for weight loss in overweight adults 18 years and older with a reduced-calorie, low-fat diet

dosage.t: Three times daily with each main meal containing fat
dosage.n: Take during or up to 1 hour after the meal; omit dose if a meal is missed or contains no fat

dosage.t: With each fat-containing meal, up to 3 capsules daily
dosage.n: For overweight adults 18+; do not exceed 3 capsules/day

dosage.d: One daily multivitamin (with fat-soluble vitamins A, D, E, K)
dosage.t: At bedtime, >=2 h before or after orlistat
dosage.n: Recommended because orlistat reduces fat-soluble vitamin absorption

admin: Take with or up to 1 hour after each main meal containing fat
If a meal is missed or contains no fat, the dose may be omitted
Distribute daily fat, carbohydrate, and protein over three main meals; aim for ~30% of calories from fat
Take a fat-soluble vitamin supplement at least 2 hours before or after orlistat (e.g., at bedtime)
If on cyclosporine, give cyclosporine 3 hours after orlistat; if on levothyroxine, separate doses by at least 4 hours
moa: Reversible inhibitor of gastrointestinal lipases; forms a covalent bond with the active serine site of gastric and pancreatic lipases in the stomach and small-intestine lumen, inactivating them so dietary triglycerides are not hydrolyzed to absorbable free fatty acids and monoglycerides. The unabsorbed fat (~25-30%) is excreted in stool, producing a caloric deficit.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to orlistat or any ingredient
Concurrent cyclosporine (OTC label: do not use)
Organ transplant recipients (OTC label: interferes with anti-rejection drugs)
relative: History of gallbladder problems, kidney stones, or pancreatitis
History of hyperoxaluria or calcium oxalate nephrolithiasis
Patients on warfarin or seizure medication
monitor: Liver function if symptoms suggest injury

preg: Not recommended in pregnancy; weight loss offers no benefit during pregnancy and may cause fetal harm (OTC label: do not use if pregnant).
lact: Not recommended during breastfeeding; it is unknown whether orlistat is excreted in human milk (OTC label: do not use if breastfeeding).
renal: Use with caution; cases of oxalate nephropathy and acute kidney injury have been reported, particularly in patients with predisposing risk factors. No specific dose adjustment defined.
hepatic: Use with caution; rare reports of severe liver injury. Discontinue and evaluate if itching, jaundice, dark urine, or loss of appetite occurs. Contraindicated in cholestasis.

major: Cyclosporine (reduced cyclosporine levels - separate by 3 h; OTC label contraindicates)
moderate: Warfarin and other anticoagulants (altered vitamin K absorption - monitor INR)
Fat-soluble vitamins A, D, E, K and beta-carotene (reduced absorption)
Antidiabetic drugs (dose may need adjustment with weight loss)
minor: Oral contraceptives (reduced efficacy possible with severe diarrhea)
interactions.food: Take with fat-containing meals; high-fat meals worsen GI adverse effects. Limit dietary fat to ~30% of calories.
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor INR in patients on warfarin; thyroid function if on levothyroxine.

common: Oily spotting and flatus with discharge
serious: Severe or continuous abdominal pain (possible pancreatitis)
rare: Hypersensitivity reactions (pruritus, rash, urticaria, angioedema, anaphylaxis)

monitoring: Body weight and BMI response (most weight loss occurs in first 6 months)
Liver function tests if symptoms of hepatic injury appear
Renal function and urinary oxalate in patients at risk for stones
Thyroid function in patients on levothyroxine
Blood glucose/HbA1c in diabetics (adjust antidiabetic therapy as weight falls)
counsel: Take one capsule with each main meal that contains fat; skip the dose if you skip a meal or it has no fat
Follow a reduced-calorie diet with about 30% of calories from fat to limit GI side effects
Expect oily stools, gas, and possible leakage, especially with high-fat meals; these lessen on a low-fat diet
Take a daily multivitamin at bedtime (at least 2 hours apart from orlistat)
Stop and see a doctor if you develop itching, yellow skin/eyes, dark urine, loss of appetite, or severe abdominal pain
Do not use if you have had an organ transplant or take cyclosporine without medical advice
pk: Local GI effect within ~24-48 h (stool fat increase)
Minimal systemic absorption; plasma levels often undetectable
Lipase inhibition during GI transit; effect ends when drug cleared from gut
20-25 C; protect from excessive light, humidity, and temperatures over 30 C
pearls: Blocks ~25-30% of dietary fat absorption; efficacy depends on dietary fat content
GI side effects are a feature, not a bug - they signal dietary non-adherence and improve on a low-fat diet
Separate levothyroxine by >=4 h and cyclosporine by 3 h to avoid malabsorption
Always co-prescribe a bedtime fat-soluble vitamin supplement
Negligible systemic exposure makes systemic toxicity uncommon, but monitor for rare hepatic and renal events
Adjust antidiabetic and antihypertensive therapy as weight decreases
missed: If you miss a dose with a meal, take it within 1 hour of that meal; otherwise skip it and resume at the next fat-containing meal. Do not double up. Omit the dose entirely if the meal is skipped or fat-free.
overdose: Single doses up to 800 mg and chronic 240 mg TID dosing have shown no significant adverse findings; systemic effects would be expected to be reversible. In case of significant overdose, observe for 24 hours and provide supportive care; contact a poison control center.
